clue.text: Watch one's opponent in this event?

definitions.text: Watch one's opponent in this event?

parts.words: Watch one's opponent in this event?
parts.note: in this cycling or running race each rider goes alone against the clock, so the only rival is a watch

explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' reads as a verb telling you to keep an eye on a rival, but it is the noun: the stopwatch is the opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A race against the clock, with competitors starting separately and ranked by elapsed time.

clue.text: Girl getting up when ready

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the words for 'when' and 'ready' are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go' or 'all set'

explanation.surface: A girl rises from bed only when she is fully prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting up' turns the whole run AS SET backwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A female forename, so the clue's 'girl' is satisfied by any girl's name.

clue.text: Man who photographed contestants beneath unusual revolving stadium

indicators.note: in a down light, the photographer and the contestants sit below the turned word for 'unusual'
turning round means the word for 'unusual' is written backwards

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unusual
Man Ray was the American surrealist photographer, so the 'Man' who took photographs is Ray
the field is all the runners or competitors in a race

explanation.surface: A photographer snaps competitors under a strange rotating arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns RUM to MUR, placed above RAY and FIELD. MURRAYFIELD is the Edinburgh home of Scottish rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The national rugby union ground of Scotland, in Edinburgh, a large sports arena.

clue.text: Method of drawing water down middle of drain

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or dilute, to soften the strength of something

indicators.note: the central letter of the word drain is taken

explanation.surface: Instructions for pulling water down through the centre of a plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' suggests drawing off water, but it means making pictures; 'middle of' takes A from drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting technique using pigment bound in egg yolk, a way of making pictures.

clue.text: One printed novel in bold

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: new or fresh, so the letters of printed are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A single published novel described as daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book that was printed, but it signals a rearrangement of PRINTED into NTREPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and daring; bold as an adjective describing a brave person.

clue.text: The opposite of ground attack

definitions.meaning: grounding an aircraft stops it flying, so the reverse is allowing it into the air
to lash out verbally or physically, to fire off at someone

explanation.surface: Air power is the reverse of a ground offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means release or allow to fly, and also to launch an angry outburst at someone.

clue.text: Cover pitch or floor

definitions.meaning: a loose blanket or rug draped over a sofa or bed
to hurl or toss a ball
to disconcert or knock someone off balance, as in 'the question floored him'

explanation.surface: A decorator debates whether to carpet the playing area or the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' and 'floor' look like surfaces to cover; each is a separate sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A blanket draped over furniture; to hurl; to disconcert someone: three meanings of one word.

clue.text: Couple we love, most unusually

indicators.note: in an unusual order, so the letters of we, O and most are shuffled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A partner says their relationship is remarkably affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges WE, O and MOST together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair of people, two together, as a couple or duo.

clue.text: Tell-tale sign: time to erase mark

indicators.note: the letter for time comes in and wipes out the letter for the old currency, taking its place

parts.note: the Ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac
M stands for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A giveaway clue that it is time to rub out a blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell-tale sign' looks like one phrase but splits: 'sign' is Aries the ram, with T replacing M.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer or sneak, someone who tells on others, is slang for a betrayer.

clue.text: Don't go giving out a hot treat to bear!

indicators.note: letting go of, so the letter A is dropped from the word for 'don't go'

parts.note: wait! is a plea for someone not to leave
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
to stand someone a drink is to treat them

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a friend to stay and dish out a spicy snack to a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving out' removes A from WAIT, leaving WIT. 'bear' is the verb, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure or resist; to put up with something without giving way.

clue.text: Theatre-goer's outside amidst returning characters from Greek play

indicators.note: the outer letters sit in the middle of the turned Greek letters
coming back, so the Greek letters are read from right to left

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and mus is its plural

indicators.note: the outer letters, first and last, of theatre-goer are taken

explanation.surface: A theatre-goer stands outside among people coming back from a Greek drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns MUS to SUM; 'outside' takes T and R from theatre-goer, which go into SUM. 'play' is the verb for guitar strumming.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to play a guitar by sweeping across the strings.

clue.text: Computing pro volunteers to cut off alcohol in revenge

indicators.note: the computing, pro and volunteer pieces cut into the teetotal letters, splitting them apart

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who is off alcohol
IT is information technology, computing
for means in favour of, pro
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A tech expert volunteers to give up drink as payback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts IT FOR TA between the T and T of TT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation in kind, an equivalent blow returned for one received, a form of vengeance.

clue.text: At ball guards flourish weapons: that's novel!

indicators.note: the two letters of 'At' stand either side of the word for flourish, shielding it

parts.note: to fare well is to thrive or flourish
a ball is round, the shape of the letter O
arms are weapons

explanation.surface: At a dance, security men wave their guns about, which is a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guards' puts FAREWELL inside AT. Hemingway's 1929 war novel is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway's First World War book, a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Landing place in costume series, appearing regularly as old revolutionary

parts.note: a robe is a garment, a form of costume

indicators.note: the landing place sits inside the alternate letters of series
every other letter, starting with the first, of series is taken

parts.note: a pier is a jetty where boats land

explanation.surface: A jetty used as the set for a costume drama shown at regular intervals, about an old rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes S, R, E from series; PIER goes inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Maximilien Robespierre was a leader of the French Revolution and the Reign of Terror.

clue.text: Unexpectedly, rain beginning to flood mine beneath one

indicators.note: in an unexpected order, so the letters of rain and the initial of flood are rearranged
the opening letter of flood is taken

parts.note: a dig is an excavation, like a mine

explanation.surface: A sudden downpour starts to flood a mine shaft under someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpectedly' rearranges RAIN plus F into INFRA. 'beneath one' looks like part of the mine image but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Latin infra dignitatem, below one's dignity, unworthy of a person's status.

clue.text: Opera one set around The King And I — a new one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the word for set is placed round the king and I

parts.note: to put something is to set it down
R stands for rex, Latin for king
again the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: An opera house stages The King and I with a fresh production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King And I' looks like the musical title, but gives R and I inside PUT. The answer is Bellini's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellini's 1835 opera about Puritans and Royalists in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Republic receiving billions in endless instalments

indicators.note: taking in, so the trimmed story word holds the letter for billions
the final letter of the word for instalments is cut off

parts.note: a serial is a story told in instalments
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: A country takes on billions of debt paid in never-ending instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims SERIAL to SERIA, which takes in B.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan country governed as a republic, with Belgrade as its capital.

clue.text: Old clan that makes a ring of tents?

definitions.text: Old clan that makes a ring of tents?

parts.words: Old clan that makes a ring of tents?
parts.note: a Scottish Highland family; split in two, the name is a tented site plus something that rings

explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests a circle of tents, but a bell rings, so a camp that rings is a campsite with a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish Highland family, chiefs of which were the Dukes of Argyll.

clue.text: This is neither settled nor wholly opportune, as yet

indicators.note: not complete, so the answer is a run of letters within opportune, as yet

explanation.surface: Something is neither fixed nor entirely convenient just yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nor wholly' points to a part of the words, found across 'opportUNE AS Yet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious and unsettled; something not at rest or at ease is restless and troubled.

clue.text: English invading watched entire division appearing in waves

indicators.note: the letter for English pushes into the word for watched

parts.note: saw is the past tense of see
all means the whole, entire

explanation.surface: English troops invade, watching a whole army division arrive in waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'division' suggests an army unit, but it is a barrier dividing land from sea; 'invading' puts E inside SAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall built along a coast as a barrier, separating the land from the sea's waves.

clue.text: See daughter set about a deer and beat it

indicators.note: placed around, so V and D are put either side of the other pieces

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references
a moose is a large deer

explanation.surface: A father tells a reader to watch his daughter attack a deer and hit it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it' reads as a further assault on the deer, but is slang for leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang from Spanish 'vamos', meaning left in a hurry; to get out quickly.

clue.text: May perhaps head off, then I get moving

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: May is an example of a month
the ego is the self, the I

explanation.surface: Someone might set out, then get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' reads as 'might', but it is the month; removing M leaves ONTH. 'then' and 'get' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy and active, constantly on the move, never staying still.

clue.text: One taking direct flight landing up around E European city

indicators.note: the turned abbreviation alights inside the bird's word

parts.note: the shortest route is 'as the crow flies', so a crow takes a direct flight

indicators.note: in a down light, the abbreviation for around is read upwards

parts.note: CA is short for circa, around

explanation.surface: A passenger on a nonstop flight lands near an Eastern European city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CA to AC, which lands inside CROW. Cracow (Kraków) is in southern Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: An older English spelling of Kraków, the historic Polish city.

clue.text: Park erroneously associated with indirection and illusion

indicators.note: wrongly, so the letters of park and indirection are rearranged

explanation.surface: A park mistakenly linked with misdirection and conjuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erroneously' rearranges PARK and INDIRECTION together; 'associated with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary conjuring feat in which a rope rises unsupported, a famous magic trick.

clue.text: Laurels line lounge for audience

indicators.note: for listeners, so the words are as heard rather than written

parts.note: a line is a queue and to lounge is to doss, said together

explanation.surface: Honours given for a queue relaxing in front of an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEUE plus DOSS (British slang for lazing) sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurels are honours or praise, and the answer means prestige and acclaim.

clue.text: Mass shooting down in which a revolutionary's filled with lead shielding gangster

indicators.note: the outer pieces have the lead-and-gangster block put into them

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: the word for lead encloses the gangster

parts.note: the van is the leading position, the vanguard
Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A massacre where a radical is pumped full of bullets while protecting a mobster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass shooting' looks like a massacre, but a mass shoots down a mountain. VAN shields AL, which fills A + CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large mass of snow sliding rapidly down a mountainside.

clue.text: A gracious lady

parts.note: 'my!' and 'gracious!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A kind and refined woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' looks like an adjective, but it is the exclamation 'gracious me', meaning 'my!'
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so any woman bearing this forename.

clue.text: Report of royal flush was incorrect

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher of the Queen
to flush is to go red in the face

explanation.surface: A poker player declares a royal flush, but was mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal flush' is a poker hand, but ER (Elizabeth Regina) plus RED (a blush) give the answer; 'Report of' merely says the clue gives the account of those words.
explanation.definitionFit: Made a mistake, got it wrong, past tense of the verb to make an error.

clue.text: Ordered leaderless Liberals to make the country work!

indicators.note: without its first letter, so the tidy word loses its opening

parts.note: tidy means neat and in order
L stands for Liberal, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A political slogan urging leaderless Liberals to get the nation working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' suggests the nation, but it is countryside; the answer is a rustic poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A short poem describing rustic or pastoral life, a piece of writing about rural scenes.

clue.text: Constitutional action from Lord's producing quick wins

parts.note: a constitutional is a walk taken for one's health
Lord's is the London cricket ground, and cricket is played in overs of six balls

explanation.surface: Lord's cricket ground produces rapid victories under the constitution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' looks political but is a health walk. Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; an over is a set of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy victories gained without real opposition, often by default.
